_comment: The one place a task file's vocabulary is defined. Two consumers read it:
bin/_lint.py, which validates what is already committed, and the MCP
server at packages/worklog-memory-mcp/server.js, which builds new task
files and constrains what an agent may write.
Before this file, each side kept its own copy. _lint.py accepted 19 kinds
and server.js hardcoded 8, so 11 kinds valid in the vault were unreachable
through the MCP. Measured 2026-09-17: writing a plan into the vault, two of
ten memory_task_create calls were rejected for kinds ('test' was never
valid, 'chore' should map to cleanup) while the drift hid which of the two
Statuses are TWO sets on purpose, and a single merged list would be a test
that certifies nothing. 'valid' is what may exist in a committed file.
'agent_writable' is what a tool may set directly. They differ by exactly
one member, and that exclusion carries a reason below.
kinds_note: Additive per AGENTS.md (Liskov): legacy values stay valid and shipped files are not force-rewritten. Prefer bug -> debug/bugfix, perf -> impl/infra, tooling -> infra for new tasks.

excluded_from_agent_writable.archived: Terminal state. Reaching it also moves the file from active/ to archive/, so setting the frontmatter alone leaves the task in the wrong directory. Use the archive path (bin/archive.sh, or the memory_archive tool) which does both.

statuses_note: 'ready' sits between draft and in-progress: scope is settled and the task is claimable, where draft means scope is still shifting. Added 2026-09-16 after 21 committed task files already used it and lint errored on all 21 — the practice was ahead of the list, not wrong.
